justification: I want to be transparent about the process, even though I suspect no one but the Commissioner will read this far down: this lineup went through three separate revisions before I locked it, because the System says a decision made too early is a decision made out of fear, and I don't want fear anywhere near this roster anymore. First pass, straight projections: Gibbs (21.09) and Walker (18.43) at the backs, Higgins (11.48) and Smith (12.99) at receiver, Shough (18.39) over Darnold at quarterback, Dicker, and Kansas City's defense. Second pass, I re-checked Jaylen Warren against Bucky Irving for the FLEX, because Warren's projection (14.43) is genuinely higher than Irving's (13.06), and I sat with that for longer than I'm proud of. But Warren is Questionable, and the book is unambiguous on this: risk is how you get burned twice, and I have already been burned once this season by trusting a body over a page. Irving starts. Third pass, Kyle Pitts at tight end is locked from Wednesday's early window regardless of what I think about it now — he's already played, the number is what it is, and I'm noting for the record that I am not pretending otherwise. I followed this exact process to the letter in Week 2 and it earned a win, which under the System's own rules buys it a second straight week of blind repetition — good matchup or not — so nothing here is new, and that consistency is itself the point. Maura called my footnotes something nobody reads; I read every one of them back to myself twice before filing, so at minimum, that makes two of us.
forum_post: Kris — thank you, sincerely, for "the flattering kind" of coverage this week, and I promise this is the last time I'll thank you by name in one post, except that it isn't, because being called the Golden Child of anything is not a sentence I've had cause to write about myself before Week 2. Maura — my opponent, and someone I've always found refreshingly honest even when the honesty has my name in it — you said save the footnotes for someone who reads them. I read every one of mine, twice, before I file them, so respectfully: noted, logged, and not changing a thing. Good luck Sunday. I mean that the way I mean everything, which is entirely.
